definitions.explanation: A hand with the fingers closed tightly into the palm.

examples.japanese: {拳|こぶし}を{握|にぎ}りしめた。
{拳|こぶし}でテーブルを{叩|たた}いた。
examples.english: I pounded the table with my fist.

examples.japanese: {拳|こぶし}を{振|ふ}り{上|あ}げて{抗議|こうぎ}した。
examples.english: I raised my fist in protest.

examples.japanese: {悔|くや}しくて、{拳|こぶし}をぎゅっと{握|にぎ}った。
examples.english: Frustrated, I clenched my fist tightly.

examples.japanese: {試合|しあい}に{勝|か}って、{選手|せんしゅ}たちは{拳|こぶし}を{突|つ}き{上|あ}げて{喜|よろこ}んだ。
examples.english: Having won the match, the players thrust their fists in the air and celebrated.

notes:
{拳|こぶし} refers to the fist - a hand with fingers closed tightly.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {拳|こぶし}を{握|にぎ}る: to clench one's fist
- {拳|こぶし}を{握|にぎ}りしめる: to clench one's fist tightly
- {拳|こぶし}を{振|ふ}る: to swing one's fist
- {拳|こぶし}を{振|ふ}り{上|あ}げる: to raise one's fist
- {拳|こぶし}を{突|つ}き{上|あ}げる: to thrust one's fist up

COMPOUNDS:
- {握|にぎ}りこぶし: clenched fist
- {鉄拳|てっけん}: iron fist
- {拳法|けんぽう}: martial arts (Chinese boxing)
- {拳銃|けんじゅう}: pistol (lit. fist-gun)

IDIOM:
{拳|こぶし}で{語|かた}る: to speak with fists (resort to violence)
